transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I'm here because of my eating. It's just... once I start eating those comfort foods, I tell myself, 'Maria, that is enough.' But then my hand just goes right back to the pot. It's like I just can't make myself stop.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yes, I suppose I do. Some afternoons... well, like after choir or working out in the garden, I'll fix myself a plate of rice and beans, or maybe some chicken stew. And then I just keep going back for more. I don't stop until I've eaten enough for two or three meals, all at once.
After you eat that much, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to get rid of the food?
Oh, no. No, I've never done anything like that. I just... well, I just sit there feeling awfully full and upset with myself. But I never try to make myself throw up.
When that happens, do you feel unable to stop eating once you've started?
Yes, that's exactly it. Like I mentioned earlier, I'll tell myself to stop, but I just can't. My hand just keeps going back for more, and I feel like I have no control over it once I get started.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?

I don't know if I'd call it a lot of distress. I mean... I do feel upset with myself right after, like I mentioned. And a bit foolish for eating so much. But it doesn't ruin my whole day or keep me up at night or anything like that. I mostly just feel too full and wish I had stopped sooner.
When these overeating episodes happen, do they cause you marked distress?

Well, like I was just saying a moment ago, no, I wouldn't call it marked. I mean, I feel a bit foolish and uncomfortable right after it happens, sure. But it's not something that completely upsets me or stays with me. I just feel bad about it for a little bit and then I move on.
During these eating episodes, do you eat much more quickly than you normally do?

Yes, I do. I've actually always been a pretty slow eater my whole life. But lately, when this happens, I eat very fast. I'll just be standing there by the kitchen counter, and... well, I'm hardly even tasting the food before the next bite is already in my mouth.
During those episodes, do you keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yes, I do. By the time I finally stop eating, my stomach just feels... well, tight and heavy. It gets to the point where I have to go sit in my recliner and loosen my waistband because I definitely went way past what felt comfortable.
During these episodes, do you eat even when you’re not physically hungry?

No, I wouldn't say so. I usually wait until my stomach is actually growling before I get anything. I mean, I am genuinely hungry when I begin eating... it's just that I end up eating way too much once I get going. But I don't really start eating if I'm not hungry to begin with.
When these overeating episodes happen, do you usually eat alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you’re eating?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I live by myself, so I'm usually alone anyway. But I don't try to hide it or anything. If my family is over visiting, I don't go off to another room to eat or wait for them to leave. I'm not really embarrassed about it like that, it's just something that happens.
After these episodes, do you feel disgusted with yourself?

Yes... I do. After it's over, I just feel really ashamed and sad. You know, food always used to mean family and caring for each other. And now... well, I feel like I've turned it into something I have to hide from the people at my church.
How often do these overeating episodes happen?

Well, since my friend passed away, I'd say it's been happening most weeks. Usually just once or twice a week. It mostly seems to happen on those quiet afternoons... you know, like after I get back from choir practice, or when I finish up my gardening for the day.
For how many months have these overeating episodes been happening once or twice a week?
It's been going on for about three months now. Like I said, it all started right after my close friend passed away.
